gatadiso.meaning_2: who has reached the goal; who has attained the final destination; one whose direction is fulfilled
gatadiso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound of gata (gone, reached) and disa (direction, quarter), used as an epithet of an arahant in a stock description; nominative singular in the text. Spelling varies gatadiso / gatadisa; cf. gataddha and gatakoṭi in the same list.
gatadiso.example_1: so vutthavāso ciṇṇacaraṇo gataddho gatadiso gatakoṭiko pālitabrahmacariyo uttamadiṭṭhippatto bhāvitamaggo, pahīnakileso paṭividdhākuppo sacchikatanirodho.
gatadiso.example_2: so vuṭṭhavāso ciṇṇacaraṇo gataddho gatadiso gatakoṭiko pālitabrahmacariyo uttamadiṭṭhippatto bhāvitamaggo pahīnakileso paṭividdhākuppo sacchikatanirodho, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, maggo bhāvito, nirodho sacchikato, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ.

pettivisayikoti.meaning_2: one belonging to the realm of the departed; a being in the ghost realm; a dweller in the world of the petas
pettivisayikoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ti (-iti) and quoted as a designation of beings; nominative singular. The word is a bahubbīhi-type adjective used as a noun. First member is petti (from peta) + visaya.
pettivisayikoti.example_1: nerayikoti vā tiracchānayonikoti vā pettivisayikoti vā manussoti vā devoti vā rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā, so hetu natthi paccayo natthi kāraṇaṃ natthi yena vadeyyuṃ katheyyuṃ bhaṇeyyuṃ dīpeyyuṃ vohareyyunti—
pettivisayikoti.example_2: nerayikoti vā tiracchānayonikoti vā pettivisayikoti vā manussoti vā devoti vā rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā.

visajjaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the phrase sajjaṃ visajjaṃ (paired with sajja), describing a vehicle left loose and released. Could also be analysed as a contraction of visajjetvā, but here it agrees with sajjaṃ.
visajjaṃ.example_1: yathā yānaṃ vā vayhaṃ vā rathaṃ vā sakaṭaṃ vā sandamānikaṃ vā sajjaṃ visajjaṃ karonti vikopenti—
visajjaṃ.example_2: yathā vayhaṃ vā rathaṃ vā sakaṭaṃ vā sandamānikaṃ vā sajjaṃ visajjaṃ karonti vikopenti;

upalakkhayitvā.meaning_2: having noticed; having observed; having made a mental note
upalakkhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā; in the text it follows other participles such as sutvā and upadhāretvā. The form is upalakkhayitvā, from the causative base upalakkhaya; the root is √lakkh.
upalakkhayitvā.example_1: sutvānahaṃ vīramakāmakāminti sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhāretvā upalakkhayitvā.
upalakkhayitvā.example_2: sutvāna nāgassa apanamissanti itoti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ byappathaṃ desanaṃ anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhaṃ sutvā suṇitvā uggahetvā upadhārayitvā upalakkhayitvā ito apanamissanti vajissanti pakkamissanti disāvidisaṃ gamissantīti—

yāpayatoti.meaning_2: causes to go; keeps going; maintains; sustains; lives
yāpayatoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √yā. In the text it is part of a string of synonyms for walking, living, moving about: iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayato. The -ti is the quotation marker ti, so the headword is the verb form yāpayati. Related causative forms are yāpeti and yapayati.
yāpayatoti.example_1: kathaṃ satassa caratoti kathaṃ satassa sampajānassa carato viharato iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayatoti—
yāpayatoti.example_2: evaṃ satassa caratoti evaṃ satassa sampajānassa carato viharato iriyato vattayato pālayato yapayato yāpayatoti—

upasantiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is accusative singular, paired with santi and vūpasanti (santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ). From upa + santa, the past participle of upasammati; the PEU entry upasanta gives 'calmness'.
upasantiṃ.example_1: makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ kittayissāmi pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—
upasantiṃ.example_2: ajjhattasantiṃ ajjhattaṃ rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭipassaddhiṃ santiṃ.

vūpasantiṃ.meaning_2: complete peace; appeasement; relief; calmed state
vūpasantiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a series with santiṃ, upasantiṃ, nibbutiṃ, paṭippassaddhiṃ. Sometimes written vūpasama; the reading here points to a feminine noun santi with the vi+upa prefix.
vūpasantiṃ.example_1: makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭippassaddhiṃ kittayissāmi pakittayissāmi ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi uttānīkarissāmi pakāsissāmīti—
vūpasantiṃ.example_2: ajjhattasantiṃ ajjhattaṃ rāgassa santiṃ, dosassa santiṃ, mohassa santiṃ, kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … sabbakilesānaṃ … sabbaduccaritānaṃ … sabbadarathānaṃ … sabbapariḷāhānaṃ … sabbasantāpānaṃ … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santiṃ upasantiṃ vūpasantiṃ nibbutiṃ paṭipassaddhiṃ santiṃ.

hanusañcopano.meaning_2: movement of the jaw; grinding of the teeth
hanusañcopano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as hanusañcopano, with a variant nasal (cf. the PEU's hanasuṃ copana). Nominative singular.
hanusañcopano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho mukhakulānavikulānamatto hoti, na ca tāva hanusañcopano hoti.

disāvidisānuvilokano.meaning_2: looking around in all directions; glancing in every direction
disāvidisānuvilokano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominalised compound functioning as a predicate nominative in the sentence; describes the stage of anger when one has not yet begun looking around.
disāvidisānuvilokano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho pharusavācaṃ nicchāraṇamatto hoti, na ca tāva disāvidisānuvilokano hoti.

daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.meaning_2: striking with rod and sword; coming to blows with stick and weapon
daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nominative singular describing the stage of anger. The printed form has a single b (daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano), which is likely a spelling for daṇḍasatthābhinipātano; sandhi of sattha + abhinipātana.
daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano.example_1: atthi kañci kālaṃ kodho daṇḍasatthaabbhukkiraṇamatto hoti, na ca tāva daṇḍasatthaabhinipātano hoti.

santiphusanāya.meaning_2: touching peace; attainment of peace; experiencing of peace
santiphusanāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative singular in the text. Part of a triplet with santādhigama and santisacchikiriyā, meaning the realisation of Nibbāna.
santiphusanāya.example_1: athāparenākārena ye dhammā santādhigamāya santiphusanāya santisacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti, seyyathidaṃ—
santiphusanāya.example_2: atha aparena ākārena ye dhammā santādhigamāya santiphusanāya santisacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti, seyyathidaṃ—

pādaloliyena.meaning_2: restlessness of feet; footlooseness; wandering about
pādaloliyena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun formed from pādalola. In the text it appears in the instrumental singular: 'pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti' = 'possessed of footlooseness'. Some analyses may treat it as adj agreeing with bhikkhu, but the neuter abstract noun fits best.
pādaloliyena.example_1: idhekacco bhikkhu pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti—
pādaloliyena.example_2: atha vā bhikkhu antosaṅghārāme pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti, na atthahetu na kāraṇahetu uddhato avūpasantacitto pariveṇato pariveṇaṃ gacchati, vihārato vihāraṃ gacchati, aḍḍhayogato aḍḍhayogaṃ gacchati, pāsādato pāsādaṃ gacchati, hammiyato hammiyaṃ gacchati, guhato guhaṃ gacchati, leṇato leṇaṃ gacchati, kuṭiyā kuṭiṃ gacchati, kūṭāgārato kūṭāgāraṃ gacchati, aṭṭato aṭṭaṃ gacchati, māḷato māḷaṃ gacchati, uddaṇḍato uddaṇḍaṃ gacchati, upaṭṭhānasālato upaṭṭhānasālaṃ gacchati, maṇḍapato maṇḍapaṃ gacchati, rukkhamūlato rukkhamūlaṃ gacchati, yattha vā pana bhikkhū nisīdanti vā gacchanti vā, tattha ekassa vā dutiyo hoti, dvinnaṃ vā tatiyo hoti, tiṇṇaṃ vā catuttho hoti.

pādaloliyā.meaning_2: unsteadiness of the feet; restlessness of the feet; wandering about
pādaloliyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] pāda + lola + suffix ṇiya (see PEU), hence nt abstract noun. The form pādaloliyā in the text is ablative singular, 'away from restlessness of the feet', parallel to ārato. The compound pādalola occurs in the quoted phrase na ca pādalolo. Some analyses take pādaloliyā as fem.
pādaloliyā.example_1: na ca pādaloloti so paccekasambuddho pādaloliyā ārato virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgāraṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto sadatthagarukoti—
pādaloliyā.example_2: pādaloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, pādaloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyya careyya vicareyya iriyeyya vatteyya pāleyya yapeyya yāpeyya, paṭisallānārāmo assa paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto paramatthagarukoti—

parikeḷanā.meaning_2: play; amusement; dalliance; fondness for adornment
parikeḷanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of a monastic's vain adornments, following keḷanā; the variant gedhitatā/gedhitattaṃ appears in some editions. Nominative singular in the text.
parikeḷanā.example_1: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—
parikeḷanā.example_2: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gedhitatā gedhitattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—

uppāṭayitvā.meaning_2: having pulled out; having torn out; having uprooted; having eradicated
uppāṭayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive, part of a series of synonyms (uddharitvā, samuddharitvā, pajahitvā) for eradicating a defilement. Sometimes analysed with √paṭh (paṭh + *aya), but √paṭ 1 is preferred here.
uppāṭayitvā.example_1: attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—
uppāṭayitvā.example_2: tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṅkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.

visaritaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular agreeing with taṇhājāliniṃ; visaritaṃ visattikaṃ describes the craving-net as spread out and clinging.
visaritaṃ.example_1: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenakaṃ namuciṃ kaṇhaṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhametvā ca taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahi vinodesi byantīakāsi anabhāvaṅgamesi.
visaritaṃ.example_2: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenaṃ kaṇhaṃ namuciṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhamitvā taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahasi vinodesi byantiṃ akāsi anabhāvaṃ gamesi.

sambujjhitabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be fully understood; to be comprehended; to be awakened to
sambujjhitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the Niddesa alongside bujjhitabba, anubujjhitabba, paṭibujjhitabba. Neuter nominative singular in the text.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_1: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ tena bodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsi.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_2: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ tena paccekabodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsīti evaṃ so paccekasambuddho eko anuttaraṃ paccekasambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti—

paṭivinoditvā.meaning_2: having driven away; having dispelled; having removed
paṭivinoditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of vippajahitvā in these verses; the absolutive of paṭivinodeti, formed from the past participle stem paṭivinodita. No simplex paṭivinodati is attested.
paṭivinoditvā.example_1: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.)] paṇḍitā, viharanti te vigatarajassa sāsane.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_1: having abandoned this dust, the wise dwell in the Dispensation of the dustless one.
paṭivinoditvā.example_2: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.) mahāni.209] cakkhumā, tasmā jino vigatarajoti vuccati.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_2: Since the Clear-eyed One has abandoned this corruption, the Victorious Buddha is called ‘one whose corruption has faded away.’

puramāhiyati.meaning_2: Pura (city) and Māhissati (name of a city); to the city of Māhissatī
puramāhiyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text for puramāhissati; the second element is probably the name Māhissatī rather than a verb, though the spelling with -y- is irregular.
puramāhiyati.translation_1: 36. They went to Patiṭṭhāna of the city of Aḷaka, then to Māhissati,

pimpati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for lippati at this line, glossed by the commentary as sticking or being smeared. 3rd singular present in the text.
pimpati.example_1: Ko ubhantamabhiññāya, majjhe mantā na lippati [na pimpati (bahūsu)];
pimpati.translation_1: Who, having comprehended the two ends, is not stuck in the middle with wisdom?

yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.meaning_2: from the beginning of the Ajitamāṇavapucchā through to the end of the Pārāyanānugītigāthā
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yāva + pārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā. The second member is a compound meaning 'ending with the Pārāyanānugītigāthā'. Commentarial citation indicating a range of text, parenthesised in the manuscript; not part of the verse.
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.example_1: Addhā gamissāmi na mettha kaṅkhā, evaṃ maṃ dhārehi adhimuttacittan ’’ ti [ajitamāṇavapucchāya paṭṭhāya yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā syā.… potthake natthi].
yāvapārāyanānugītigātāpariyosānā.translation_1: I will surely go there; I have no doubt about this. Consider me one whose mind is thus inclined.”

palippati.meaning_2: is smeared (with); is stained (by); is defiled (by)
palippati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of palippati, used in the Niddesa gloss as a synonym of lippati and upalippati; the prefix pa- is intensive.
palippati.example_1: so ubhantamabhiññāya, majjhe mantā na lippatīti so ubho ca ante majjhañca mantāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā na lippati na palippati na upalippati, alitto asaṃlitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti—
palippati.example_2: So ubhantamabhiññāya , majjhe mantā na lippatīti so ubho ca ante majjhañca mantāya abhiññāya jānitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā na lippati na palippati na upalippati, alitto asaṃlitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti – so ubhantamabhiññāya majjhe mantā na lippati.
palippati.translation_2: ‘One who, having directly known both ends and the middle, is not stained by them’ means that having known, calculated, judged, clarified, and made evident both the ends and the middle with wisdom, he is not stained, not smeared, not defiled; he is untainted, escaped, released, detached, and dwells with a mind unconstrained by boundaries.

vidhūmito.meaning_2: smoke-free; freed from smoke; purged; destroyed; done away with
vidhūmito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle in -ita of vidhūmeti ('to free from smoke; to purge'), used figuratively in the Niddesa for defilements being burnt away. Appears in the text in nominative singular masculine (rāgo ... vidhūmito) and in neuter forms (kāyaduccaritaṃ ... vidhūmitaṃ), agreeing with its subject. Sometimes analysed as vidhūma + ta.
vidhūmito.example_1: manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmito.example_2: vidhūmoti kāyaduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ [byantikataṃ (ka.)], vacīduccaritaṃ … pe … manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmito.translation_2: ‘Smoke-free’ means bodily misconduct is smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free; verbal misconduct... mental misconduct... lust, hatred, delusion, anger, resentment, denigration, insolence, envy, avarice, deceit, fraud, obstinacy, rivalry, conceit, excessive conceit, intoxication, negligence, all defilements, all misconducts, all troubles, all fevers, all burnings, and all unwholesome formative actions are smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free.

vidhūmitā.meaning_2: smoke-free; freed from smoke; destroyed; cleared away
vidhūmitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the Niddesa gloss of vidhūmo, agreeing with duccarita, rāga and other masculine and neuter nouns, and in the plural with sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā.
vidhūmitā.example_1: manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmitā.example_2: vidhūmoti kāyaduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ [byantikataṃ (ka.)], vacīduccaritaṃ … pe … manoduccaritaṃ vidhūmitaṃ vidhamitaṃ sositaṃ visositaṃ byantīkataṃ, rāgo … doso … moho vidhūmito vidhamito sosito visosito byantīkato, kodho … upanāho … makkho … paḷāso … issā … macchariyaṃ … māyā … sāṭheyyaṃ … thambho … sārambho … māno … atimāno … mado … pamādo … sabbe kilesā sabbe duccaritā sabbe darathā sabbe pariḷāhā sabbe santāpā sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārā vidhūmitā vidhamitā sositā visositā byantīkatā.
vidhūmitā.translation_2: ‘Smoke-free’ means bodily misconduct is smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free; verbal misconduct... mental misconduct... lust, hatred, delusion, anger, resentment, denigration, insolence, envy, avarice, deceit, fraud, obstinacy, rivalry, conceit, excessive conceit, intoxication, negligence, all defilements, all misconducts, all troubles, all fevers, all burnings, and all unwholesome formative actions are smoke-free, destroyed, withered, fully withered, and made smoke-free.

dhammasaṅgaṇiye.meaning_2: Dhamma enumeration; Dhammasaṅgaṇī (first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka)
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the commentarial phrase dhammasaṅgaṇiye, cited as the source of the variant reading lāpo palāpo. Title of the first Abhidhamma book.
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.example_1: Paridevoti ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena vā samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena vā phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo [lāpo palāpo (syā.) dhammasaṅgaṇiye] vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ [lālappāyanā lālappāyitattaṃ (bahūsu) jarāsuttaniddesaṭṭhakathā oloketabbā].
dhammasaṅgaṇiye.translation_1: Paridevoti: of one struck by the loss of relatives ... or by any other painful phenomenon—lamentation, great lamentation, act of lamenting, great act of lamenting, state of lamenting, state of great lamenting, verbal babble, erratic babble, babbling, act of babbling, state of babbling.

dhammamuttaṃmaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of dhammamuttaman in the text, resolved as dhamma + uttamaṃ and glossed as amataṃ nibbānaṃ. Could also be read as dhammamuttaṃ + amataṃ, but the gloss points to uttamaṃ (or uttama).
dhammamuttaṃmaṃ.translation_1: “Supreme Dhamma” refers to the Deathless Nibbāna.

ākiñcanaṃ.meaning_2: having nothing; possessionless; free from worldly ties
ākiñcanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, qualifying brāhmaṇaṃ. It is a negative compound in na-a, a- + kiñcana, with lengthening of the initial vowel. The related abstract noun ākiñcañña is a different word.

pamuñcituṃ.meaning_2: to release; to set free; to let loose
pamuñcituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in a string of glosses on pamocanāya (muñcituṃ, pamuñcituṃ, mocetuṃ, pamocetuṃ ...). Causative-like sense 'to set free'. Root √muc (release, free); pa + √muc with -c- in the base.
pamuñcituṃ.example_1: nāhaṃ sahissāmi pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṅkathāsallatoti.
pamuñcituṃ.example_2: Nāhaṃ sahissāmi [samīhāmi (ka.)] pamocanāyāti nāhaṃ taṃ sakkomi muñcituṃ pamuñcituṃ mocetuṃ pamocetuṃ uddharituṃ samuddharituṃ uṭṭhāpetuṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ kathaṃkathāsallatoti.
pamuñcituṃ.translation_2: “I cannot release” means: I cannot liberate, set free, loosen, set quite free, lift up, rescue, set up, or set properly from the arrow of doubt.

akiliyamāno.meaning_2: not becoming defiled; not being soiled; not becoming stained
akiliyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for akilissamāno; alternative form akiliyamāno. Present participle, nominative singular, negated with na. See kilissati.
akiliyamāno.example_1: Yathā ākāso na rajjati lākhāya vā haliddiyā [haliddena (syā.)] vā nīliyā [nīlena (syā.)] vā mañjeṭṭhāya vā evaṃ arajjamāno adussamāno amuyhamāno akilissamānoti [akiliyamāno (syā.)]– evampi ākāsova abyāpajjamāno.
akiliyamāno.translation_1: Just as space is not stained by lacquer, turmeric, indigo, or madder, so not becoming attached, not becoming angry, not becoming deluded, and not becoming defiled—in this way too, it is “Like space, not becoming affected.”

mābhinibbattesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text mābhinibbattesi (mā + abhinibbattesi) is a prohibitive aorist-like form meaning 'do not generate'; the entry is for the present 3rd singular. Causative of abhinibbattati; cf. nibbatteti.
mābhinibbattesi.example_1: bhavābhavāyāti bhavābhavāya kammabhavāya punabbhavāya kāmabhavāya, kammabhavāya kāmabhavāya punabbhavāya rūpabhavāya, kammabhavāya rūpabhavāya punabbhavāya arūpabhavāya, kammabhavāya arūpabhavāya punabbhavāya punappunabbhavāya, punappunagatiyā punappunaupapattiyā punappunapaṭisandhiyā punappunaattabhāvābhinibbattiyā taṇhaṃ mākāsi mā janesi mā sañjanesi mā nibbattesi mābhinibbattesi, pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—
mābhinibbattesi.example_2: idaṃ kiñcanaṃ tuyhaṃ mā ahu mā ahosi mā janesi mā sañjanesi mābhinibbattesi pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—

patarituṃ.meaning_2: to cross over; to pass beyond; to traverse
patarituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of patarati, listed with synonyms tarituṃ, uttarituṃ, samatikkamituṃ in a series describing crossing the floods. Probably a variant of patarati.
patarituṃ.example_1: anissitoti puggalaṃ vā anissito dhammaṃ vā anissito no visahāmi na ussahāmi na sakkomi na paṭibalo mahantaṃ kāmoghaṃ bhavoghaṃ diṭṭhoghaṃ avijjoghaṃ tarituṃ uttarituṃ patarituṃ samatikkamituṃ vītivattitunti—
patarituṃ.example_2: Anissitoti puggalaṃ vā anissito dhammaṃ vā anissito no visahāmi na ussahāmi na sakkomi na paṭibalo mahantaṃ kāmoghaṃ bhavoghaṃ diṭṭhoghaṃ avijjoghaṃ tarituṃ uttarituṃ patarituṃ samatikkamituṃ vītivattitunti – anissito no visahāmi tārituṃ.
patarituṃ.translation_2: “Without a support” means: not relying on a person and not relying on a Dhamma, I am not able, not striving, not capable, not qualified to cross, go across, pass beyond, or fully transcend the great flood of sensual desires, the flood of existence, the flood of views, or the flood of ignorance; this is the meaning of “Without a support, I am unable to cross.”

dakkhamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of dakkhati (irregular present of √dis). Nominative singular masculine, used in a string of synonyms for seeing in the Niddesa.
dakkhamāno.example_1: nissaraṇato pekkhamāno dakkhamāno olokayamāno nijjhāyamāno upaparikkhamāno.
dakkhamāno.example_2: pekkhamānoti pekkhamāno dakkhamāno dissamāno passamāno olokayamāno nijjhāyamāno upaparikkhamānoti—

khambhitā.meaning_2: checked; restrained; held back; blocked; made stiff
khambhitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only the plural form khambhitā is found in the text, where it sits in a list of words meaning 'shaken, driven away'. The PEU entry takes the root as 'khabhi', but √khambh (prop, be stiff) is the usual analysis. Nom. pl. in the text.
khambhitā.example_1: vātavegena khittāti vātavegena khittā ukkhittā nunnā paṇunnā khambhitā vikkhambhitāti—
khambhitā.example_2: Vātavegena khittāti vātavegena khittā [khittaṃ (syā.) evamaññesu padesu niggahītantavasena] ukkhittā nunnā paṇunnā khambhitā vikkhambhitāti – acci yathā vātavegena khittā.
khambhitā.translation_2: “Cast by a gust of wind” means: shaken, extremely shaken, driven away, removed to a distance, checked, or not kept in the vicinity; thus it is “like a flame cast by a gust of wind.”

anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.meaning_2: devotion to a harsh life of many and various extreme austerities and difficult practices
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.construction: aneka + vividha + atiparama + dukkara + kārika + lūkha + jīvita + anuyoga
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Long bahubbīhi compound describing the ascetic; instrumental singular in the text, qualifying upetaṃ muniṃ. The segmentation of the middle members is uncertain (atiparama + dukkara + kārika is one possibility).
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.example_1: udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti—
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.example_2: Udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannanti udāhu anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhajīvitānuyogena upetaṃ samupetaṃ upāgataṃ samupāgataṃ upapannaṃ samupapannaṃ samannāgataṃ muniṃ vadanti kathenti bhaṇanti dīpayanti voharantīti – udāhu ve jīvitenūpapannaṃ.
anekavividhaatiparamadukkarakārikalūkhaj.translation_2: “Or do they call him one endowed with a [specific] livelihood?”: Or do they call, speak of, declare, explain, and designate a person as a sage because he is endowed with a livelihood that consists of various kinds of austerity and difficult practices—that is what is meant by ‘or do they call him one endowed with a livelihood.’

tireti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of tarati in the sense of penetrating, examining throughly. Variant reading tīreti in the text. 3rd singular present; used of judging craving by the forty aspects; tīraṇapariññā.
tireti.example_1: Evaṃ ñātaṃ katvā taṇhaṃ tīreti [tireti (syā.)] aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato ītito upaddavato bhayato upasaggato calato pabhaṅguto addhuvato atāṇato aleṇato asaraṇato asaraṇībhūtato rittato tucchato suññato anattato ādīnavato vipariṇāmadhammato asārakato aghamūlato vadhakato vibhavato sāsavato saṅkhatato mārāmisato jātidhammato jarādhammato byādhidhammato maraṇadhammato sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammato saṃkilesadhammato samudayato atthaṅgamato assādato ādīnavato nissaraṇato tīreti – ayaṃ tīraṇapariññā.
tireti.translation_1: Having made it known in this way, one judges craving as inconstant, as suffering, as a disease, as a cancer, as an arrow, as a misery, as an affliction, as alien, as a disintegration, as a calamity, as trouble, as peril, as oppression, as fluctuating, as dissolving, as transient, as shelterless, as no-shelter, as no refuge, as without protection, as empty, as bare and void, as the void, as not-self, as danger, as subject to change, as having no core, as a root of evil, as a killer, as non-existence, as tainted, as conditioned, as Māra’s bait, as subject to birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair, as subject to defilement, as having an arising, as having a passing away, as gratification, as danger, as escape—this is the full understanding as judged.

paṭippasaddhattā.meaning_2: because of being tranquillised; due to being stilled; through being calmed
paṭippasaddhattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ttā of the abstract noun paṭippasaddhatta (from paṭippassaddha, pp of paṭippassambhati), used in a list of synonyms for nibbuta. Note the spelling with single -s- here beside paṭippassaddhā in the same sentence.
paṭippasaddhattā.example_1: Abhinibbutāti rāgassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, dosassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, mohassa nibbāpitattā nibbutā, kodhassa … pe … upanāhassa … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santattā samitattā vūpasamitattā nijjhātattā nibbutattā vigatattā paṭippasaddhattā santā upasantā vūpasantā nibbutā paṭippassaddhāti – diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā.
paṭippasaddhattā.translation_1: “Extinguished” means they are extinguished because they have quenched greed, quenched hatred, quenched delusion, quenched anger, and so on, up to quenching all unwholesome volitional formations; they are peaceful, calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized; this is the meaning of “Having seen the Dhamma, they are extinguished.”
paṭippasaddhattā.example_2: Upasantāti rāgassa upasamitattā nibbāpitattā upasantā … pe … dosassa … mohassa … kodhassa … upanāhassa … pe … sabbākusalābhisaṅkhārānaṃ santattā samitattā vūpasamitattā nijjhātattā nibbutattā vigatattā paṭippasaddhattā santā upasantā vūpasantā nibbutā paṭippassaddhāti upasantā.
paṭippasaddhattā.translation_2: “Calmed” means they are calmed because greed, hatred, delusion, anger, and so on, up to all unwholesome volitional formations are calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized; they are peaceful, calmed, stilled, quenched, and tranquilized.

santāpayitvā.meaning_2: having scorched; having burned; having heated; having tormented
santāpayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative santāpeti (from √tap 1). In the texts it describes the sun scorching the earth before dispelling darkness.
santāpayitvā.example_1: yathā sūriyo tejī tejena samannāgato pathaviṃ abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā santāpayitvā sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ālokaṃ dassayitvā ākāse antalikkhe gaganapathe gacchati, evameva bhagavā ñāṇatejī ñāṇatejena samannāgato sabbaṃ abhisaṅkhārasamudayaṃ …pe…
santāpayitvā.example_2: Yathā sūriyo tejī tejena samannāgato pathaviṃ abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā santāpayitvā sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ālokaṃ dassayitvā ākāse antalikkhe gaganapathe [gamanapathe (syā.) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā] gacchati, evameva bhagavā ñāṇatejī ñāṇatejena samannāgato sabbaṃ abhisaṅkhārasamudayaṃ … pe … kilesatamaṃ avijjandhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ñāṇālokaṃ dassetvā vatthukāme parijānitvā kilesakāme pahāya abhibhuyya abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvā pariyādiyitvā madditvā carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpetīti – ādiccova pathaviṃ tejī tejasā.
santāpayitvā.translation_2: Just as the sun, possessed of heat and radiance, having overwhelmed the earth, having surged over, having surged above, having consumed, and having scorched it, having destroyed all darkness that has gone into space, having driven away the darkness, having revealed light, goes into the sky, the empty space, the path of the gods; just so, the Blessed One, possessed of the radiance of knowledge and the heat of knowledge, having destroyed the origin of all volitional formations … having destroyed the darkness of defilement and the darkness of ignorance, having revealed the light of knowledge, having fully understood the sensual objects, having abandoned the defiling sensual pleasures, having overcome, having overwhelmed, having surged over, having consumed, and having crushed them, conducts himself, dwells, continues, proceeds, guards, nourishes, and sustains himself—this is the meaning of ‘just as the sun with its heat shines while overwhelming the earth.’

saraṇībhūtato.meaning_2: as having become a refuge; as a shelter
saraṇībhūtato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative of comparison in -to, from saraṇībhūta (saraṇī + bhūta), in the series khemato ... saraṇībhūtato in the Niddesa commentary.
saraṇībhūtato.example_1: nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti—
saraṇībhūtato.example_2: Nekkhammanti sammāpaṭipadaṃ anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipadaṃ anvatthapaṭipadaṃ dhammānudhammapaṭipadaṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritaṃ indriyesu guttadvārataṃ bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ satisampajaññaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ khemato tāṇato leṇato saraṇato saraṇībhūtato abhayato accutato amatato nibbānato daṭṭhuṃ passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti – nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khemato.
saraṇībhūtato.translation_2: “Renunciation”: the path of practice, the compliant path, the non-obstructive path, the path in accordance with the goal, the path of Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, perfect conduct in virtue, guarding the doors of the faculties, moderation in eating, the practice of wakefulness, mindfulness and clear comprehension, the four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four foundations for supernormal power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the noble eightfold path, Nibbāna, and the path of practice leading to Nibbāna—having seen them as secure, as a sanctuary, as a refuge, as a protection, as having no fear, as deathless, as the unmoving, as Nibbāna, having calculated, judged, examined, clarified, and made evident—this is “Having seen renunciation as secure.”

pavijjittha.meaning_2: entered; arrived (with mā: may it not enter; may it not arrive)
pavijjittha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person singular aorist in the prohibitive phrase mā pavijjittha, parallel to mā vijjittha and mā saṃvijjittha. Probably from pa + √vis with assimilation of s to jj; the v.l. is paviṭṭha.
pavijjittha.example_1: idaṃ kiñcanaṃ tuyhaṃ mā vijjittha mā pavijjittha mā saṃvijjittha pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti—
pavijjittha.example_2: Idaṃ kiñcanaṃ [ime kiñcanā (ka.)] tuyhaṃ mā vijjittha mā pavijjittha mā saṃvijjittha pajaha vinodehi byantīkarohi anabhāvaṃ gamehīti – mā te vijjittha kiñcanaṃ.
pavijjittha.translation_2: This baggage—let it not be for you, not arrive for you, not exist for you; abandon it, cast it aside, make it to be gone, bring it to non-existence—this is “Let not such baggage be yours.”

jāguṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, listed in a string of synonyms for 'being' (satta, jana, nara, puggala, jīva). The PEU suggests an analysis jāti + gamu, but it is uncertain; possibly related to jantu.
jāguṃ.example_1: jantunti sattaṃ janaṃ naraṃ mānavaṃ posaṃ puggalaṃ jīvaṃ jāguṃ jantuṃ indaguṃ manujanti—
jāguṃ.example_2: Jantunti sattaṃ janaṃ naraṃ māṇavaṃ [mānavaṃ (syā.)] posaṃ puggalaṃ jīvaṃ jāguṃ jantuṃ indaguṃ manujanti – teneva māro anveti jantuṃ.
jāguṃ.translation_2: “The person” means the being, the man, the human, the fellow, the individual, the living being, the creature, the person, the mortal—this is the meaning of “by that, Māra follows the person.”

paṭivicāraṇaṃ.meaning_2: wandering about; roaming; going to and fro
paṭivicāraṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of a gloss explaining vicāraṇa: cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ. Nominative singular neuter, in apposition.
paṭivicāraṇaṃ.example_1: kiṃsu tassa vicāraṇanti kiṃsu tassa cāraṇaṃ vicāraṇaṃ paṭivicāraṇaṃ.

paṭivicāraṇā.meaning_2: ranging over; turning over; reflection; consideration
paṭivicāraṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from pati + vi + carati; listed among the nine vitakkas as vicāraṇā / paṭivicāraṇā. Nominative singular in the text.
paṭivicāraṇā.example_1: ime nava vitakkā lokassa cāraṇā vicāraṇā paṭivicāraṇā.

uparujjhatī.meaning_2: stops; comes to an end; ceases; is cut off
uparujjhatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of upa + √rudh 1 (obstruct, stop). The text glosses it with nirujjhati, vūpasammati, atthaṃ gacchati, paṭippassambhati. In pada 2 the finite verb stands for a relative clause with yattha.
uparujjhatī.example_2: yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatīti nāmanti cattāro arūpino khandhā.

antonimmuggaposīni.meaning_2: thriving (while) completely submerged (under water); growing underneath (the water's surface)
antonimmuggaposīni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads antonimuggaposīni (variant antonimuggaposīni); the entry takes the stem antonimuggaposī. Describes lotuses that grow entirely underwater, in contrast to those on the surface and those standing above the water. Here it is nominative plural neuter modifying uppalāni, padumāni, puṇḍarīkāni. The word is a compound of anto, nimugga, and posī.
antonimmuggaposīni.example_1: Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni antonimuggaposīni [antonimmuggaposīni (ka.)], appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakā accuggamma tiṭṭhanti anupalittāni udakena;
antonimmuggaposīni.translation_1: Just as in a pool of blue, red, or white lotuses, some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, not rising above the water, thriving underwater; some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, resting on the water's surface; and some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water, thrive in the water, and stand lifted up far above the water, untouched by it;

samuhacca.meaning_2: having completely uprooted; having entirely removed; having destroyed
samuhacca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text by uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā; variant reading uhacca samuhacca. Companion absolutive to ūhacca in the phrase attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samuhacca.
samuhacca.example_1: Attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca [uhacca samuhacca (ka.) saddanītiyā pana sameti] uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti – attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca.
samuhacca.translation_1: “Having uprooted the identity-view” means having pulled up, completely pulled up, removed, completely removed, cleared, completely cleared, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence the identity-view—thus, ‘having uprooted the identity-view.’

mohamuho.meaning_2: deluded by ignorance; confused by delusion; one whose mouth is folly
mohamuho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A bahubbīhi compound, glossed in the text as moha-mukha: 'one whose mouth is delusion'. The reading momuho is likely a misreading for mohamuho. Nominative singular in the sentence.

ītijāte.meaning_2: afflicted with calamity; fallen into distress; beset by misfortune
ītijāte.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa passage it glosses santāpajāte, describing one afflicted by illness and calamity; locative singular in the text.
ītijāte.example_1: diṭṭhibyasanena dukkhena santāpajāte ītijāte upaddavajāte upasaggajāteti—
ītijāte.example_2: Santāpajāteti jātiyā santāpajāte, jarāya santāpajāte, byādhinā santāpajāte, maraṇena santāpajāte, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi santāpajāte, nerayikena dukkhena santāpajāte … pe … diṭṭhibyasanena dukkhena santāpajāte ītijāte upaddavajāte upasaggajāteti – santāpajāte.
ītijāte.translation_2: “Tormented” means: tormented by birth, tormented by decay, tormented by illness, tormented by death, tormented by sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, tormented by the suffering of the hells... tormented by the suffering of wrong views; with illness that has arisen, with dangers that have arisen, with suffering that has arisen. This is the meaning of “tormented.”

uttānīākāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular aorist (with the ā augment) of uttānīkaroti, 'makes clear'; one item in a list of synonyms for byākāsi. Prefixed form of karoti, so the root fields are given; uttānī- corresponds to uttāna ('clear, plain') plus the denominative suffix -ī.
uttānīākāsi.example_1: pañhaṃ byākāsīti pañhaṃ byākāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīākāsi pakāsesīti—
uttānīākāsi.example_2: Pañhaṃ byākāsīti pañhaṃ byākāsi ācikkhi desesi paññapesi paṭṭhapesi vivari vibhaji uttānīākāsi pakāsesīti – ajjhiṭṭho puṭṭho puṭṭho pañhaṃ byākāsi.
uttānīākāsi.translation_2: “Answered their questions” means he answered the question, explained, taught, prepared, established, opened up, analyzed, clarified, and proclaimed. Thus: “Having been requested, and having been asked repeatedly, he answered their questions.”

vitosesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as vitosesi, the aorist 3rd singular meaning 'gladdened; pleased; delighted'. The sekhiya passage glosses tosesi with tosesi vitosesi pasādesi ārādhesi attamane akāsi, treating the forms as synonyms. For the same passage the PEU gives vitoseti [vi+tusa+ṇe+ti], causative of √tus; the form is also written vitosesi.
vitosesi.example_1: tosesīti tosesi vitosesi pasādesi ārādhesi attamane akāsi.

vitositā.meaning_2: gladdened; caused to rejoice; satisfied; delighted
vitositā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used adjectivally in the Niddesa gloss; nominative plural masculine agreeing with tositā in the text.
vitositā.example_1: tositāti tositā vitositā pasāditā ārādhitā attamanā katāti—
vitositā.example_2: Tositāti tositā vitositā pasāditā ārādhitā attamanā katāti – te tositā.
vitositā.translation_2: “Delighted” means delighted, caused to rejoice, caused to be clear, satisfied, and made joyful—this is “delighted.”

vivano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it occurs in a string of epithets of the Buddha, probably glossing nibbāna from the root √van (desire/forest) with the prefix vi-. Nominative singular.
vivano.example_1: tasmā buddho avano vivano nibbano vanāpagato vanavippahīno vanavimutto sabbavanavītivattoti—
vivano.example_2: Tasmā buddho avano vivano nibbano vanāpagato vanavippahīno vanavimutto sabbavanavītivattoti – nibbano.
vivano.translation_2: Therefore the Buddha is without forest, free from forest, gone out, gone from the forest, has abandoned the forest, is freed from the forest, and has crossed over all forests—this is “gone out.”

nitthuriyakammaṃ.meaning_2: harsh act; act of harshness; cruel deed
nitthuriyakammaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading nitthuriyakammaṃ for niṭṭhuriyakammaṃ. Nominative singular in the text, listed as a synonym of makkha.
nitthuriyakammaṃ.example_1: Makkhoti yo makkho makkhāyanā makkhāyitattaṃ niṭṭhuriyaṃ niṭṭhuriyakammaṃ [nitthuriyakammaṃ (ka.) passa vibha.892]– ayaṃ vuccati makkho.
nitthuriyakammaṃ.translation_1: “Contempt” means: whatever contempt, disparaging, disparagement, harshness, or harsh act there is—this is called contempt.

paripañhitoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of an -ti quotation ending (paripañhito ti). Past participle used passively in a list of honours paid to the Buddha: āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhito.
paripañhitoti.example_1: brahme upāsito meti so mayā bhagavā āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhitoti—
paripañhitoti.example_2: Brahme upāsito meti so mayā bhagavā āsito upāsito payirupāsito paripucchito paripañhitoti – saccavhayo brahme upāsito me.
paripañhitoti.translation_2: “I have approached, O Brahmin” means that Blessed One has been approached, attended to, deeply attended to, questioned, and cross-examined by me — this is “rightly named, I have approached, O Brahmin”.

ītippahānaṃ.meaning_2: removal of calamity; elimination of danger; abandoning of distress
ītippahānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of īti (calamity, affliction) + pahāna (abandoning). In the text it is nominative singular in a list of epithets of Nibbāna.
ītippahānaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

ītivūpasamaṃ.meaning_2: calming of distress; appeasement of calamity; pacification of affliction
ītivūpasamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of epithets of Nibbāna. Sometimes printed ītivūpassama; the second member is vūpasama (from upa + √sam 1).
ītivūpasamaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.meaning_2: relinquishment of calamity; abandoning of distress
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; part of a list of epithets of Nibbāna.
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.example_2: Ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti – taṇhakkhayamanītikaṃ.
ītipaṭinissaggaṃ.translation_2: The abandonment of trouble, the calming of trouble, the relinquishment of trouble, the complete cessation of trouble, the deathless Nibbāna — thus [it is] destruction of craving, free of trouble.

ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.meaning_2: complete cessation of trouble; calming of misfortune
ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of epithets of Nibbāna. Sometimes written ītivūpasama in the same list. The related PEU entry gives ītipaṭippassaddhi as feminine.
ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ.example_1: ītippahānaṃ ītivūpasamaṃ ītipaṭinissaggaṃ ītipaṭippassaddhiṃ amataṃ nibbānanti—

natohamasmīti.meaning_2: not so I am not (such like that); I am not like that
natohamasmīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation in the text breaks as na tiha maṃ iti, tiha being a particle variant of taha; sandhi chanda-vaṭṭa maybe uncertain, written natohamasmīti without spacing.

sampamuñcassu.meaning_2: release; let go; give up completely; place (faith)
sampamuñcassu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular imperative of sampamuñcati, glossed in the text by pamuñcassu, adhimuñcassu, okappehi; used with saddhaṃ in a series of synonyms.
sampamuñcassu.example_1: evameva tvampi pamuñcassu saddhanti evameva tvaṃ saddhaṃ muñcassu pamuñcassu sampamuñcassu adhimuñcassu okappehi.
sampamuñcassu.example_2: “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti saddhaṃ muñcassu pamuñcassu sampamuñcassu adhimuñcassu okappehi.

sammabhidevā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads sammabhidevā, a variant reading (syā.) for sammutidevā. Nominative plural in -ā in the list of three devas.
sammabhidevā.translation_1: “Devas” means there are three [types of] devas: conventional devas, born devas, and purity devas.

aphassi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the third verb of a series vedi / aññāsi / aphassi / paṭivijjhi, meaning 'knew, understood, experienced, penetrated'. The initial a- is the augment of the aorist, not a negative prefix (contrast aphassaka). Sinhala-script editions often read phassi.
aphassi.example_1: sabbaṃ vedi paroparanti bhagavā attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme vedi aññāsi aphassi paṭivijjhi.
aphassi.example_2: evaṃ bhagavā attano ca paresañca adhidevakare dhamme vedi aññāsi aphassi paṭivijjhīti—

nidveḷahakā.meaning_2: free from duplicity; without deceit; not double-tongued
nidveḷahakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the text, paired with sadveḷhaka (those who are duplicitous) and explained by nillekhā (settled). Probably a v.l. or commentarial formation for niddeḷhaka; the reading dveḷaha- for dveḷhaka- is uncertain.
nidveḷahakā.example_1: Kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷahakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti – kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānataṃ.
nidveḷahakā.translation_1: “For those who are perplexed who acknowledge” means those who are perplexed come and become free of doubt, those who are scattered come and become settled, those who have two minds come and become of one mind, those who are in doubt come and become free of doubt, those who are full of lust come and become free of lust, those who are full of hatred come and become free of hatred, those who are full of delusion come and become free of delusion, those who are defiled come and become free of defilements—that is “for those who are perplexed who acknowledge.”

adduyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for anduya/aruya, instrumental singular adduyā; the PEU gloss 'Knee' is doubtful.
adduyā.example_1: Aviheṭhayaṃ aññatarampi tesanti ekamekampi sattaṃ pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā anduyā [aruyā (syā.), adduyā (ka.)] vā rajjuyā vā aviheṭhayanto, sabbepi satte pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā anduyā vā rajjuyā vā aviheṭhayantoti – aviheṭhayaṃ aññatarampi tesaṃ.
adduyā.translation_1: “Not harming even one of them” means: not harming even one single being—whether with a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, a snare, or a rope—not harming any of all beings with a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, a snare, or a rope—this is “not harming even one of them.”

khiṭṭā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading khiṭṭā for khiḍḍā; the passage glosses it with ratī (delight). Nominative singular, subject of hoti.
khiṭṭā.example_1: 127. Khiḍḍā [khiṭṭā (ka.)] ratī hoti sahāyamajjhe , puttesu ca vipulaṃ hoti pemaṃ ;
khiṭṭā.translation_1: 127. There is playing and delight amidst companions, and there is great affection for children;

mukhabherukaṃ.meaning_2: mouth-drum; vocal drumming; making drum sounds with the mouth
mukhabherukaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of mukhakeraka in the Niddesa list of performing arts. Accusative singular in the text; part of a list of playful vocal and musical performances.
mukhabherukaṃ.example_1: Mukhabherikaṃ mukhālambaraṃ mukhaḍiṇḍimakaṃ [mukhadeṇḍimakaṃ (syā.), mukhadindimakaṃ (ka.)] mukhacalimakaṃ mukhakerakaṃ [mukhabherukaṃ (syā.)] mukhadaddarikaṃ nāṭakaṃ lāsaṃ gītaṃ davakammaṃ.
mukhabherukaṃ.translation_1: Making drum sounds with the mouth, blowing through the mouth, making trumpet sounds, tongue-clicking, making mouth-music, reciting poetry, acting, dancing, singing, and comedic skits.

hotiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text hotiṃ is a sandhi variant of hoti (before pemaṃ); the -ṃ belongs to the following word.
hotiṃ.example_1: Puttesu ca vipulaṃ hotiṃ pemanti puttesu ca adhimattaṃ hoti pemanti – puttesu ca vipulaṃ hoti pemaṃ.
hotiṃ.translation_1: “And there is great affection for children” means there is intense affection for children—and there is great affection for children.

appaṭikulā.meaning_2: not unpleasant; agreeable; pleasing; not repulsive
appaṭikulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has appaṭikulā as a variant reading of appaṭikūlā, nominative plural agreeing with sattā. The na prefix has assimilated to the following p.
appaṭikulā.example_1: Cātuddiso appaṭigho ca hotīti mettāya bhāvitattā ye puratthimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā [appaṭikulā (bahūsu)] honti, ye dakkhiṇāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye pacchimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uttarāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye puratthimāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye dakkhiṇāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye pacchimāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uttarāya anudisāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye heṭṭhimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye uparimāya disāya sattā te appaṭikūlā honti, ye disāsu vidisāsu sattā te appaṭikūlā honti;
appaṭikulā.translation_1: “Global in outlook and unobstructed” means because he has developed loving-kindness, the beings in the east, south, west, north, and the intermediate directions, as well as those below and above, are not hindered; they are not obstructed.

paṭinissatāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentary gloss, nominative singular masculine agreeing with sahitā and listed with past participles ārādhitā, ajjhottharitā, pariyāditā. The -ti at the end is a quotation marker.
paṭinissatāti.example_1: parissayānaṃ sahitāti parissaye sahitā ārādhitā ajjhottharitā pariyāditā paṭinissatāti—
paṭinissatāti.example_2: Parissayānaṃ sahitāti parissaye sahitā ārādhitā ajjhottharitā pariyāditā paṭinissatāti – parissayānaṃ sahitā.
paṭinissatāti.translation_2: “Enduring troubles” means having endured, overcome, overwhelmed, depleted, and abandoned troubles—enduring troubles.

paṭipassambhayitvāti.meaning_2: having pacified; having calmed down; having subsided
paṭipassambhayitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formation is doubtful: the Commentary glosses it with nikkhipitvā, so it is taken here as a causative absolutive of paṭipassambhati (√sambh 1), with the -aya- of the causative. The -ti belongs to the quotation (paṭipassambhayitvāti) and is not part of the word.
paṭipassambhayitvāti.example_1: oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭipassambhayitvāti—
paṭipassambhayitvāti.example_2: Oropayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭipassambhayitvāti – oropayitvā gihibyañjanāni.
paṭipassambhayitvāti.translation_2: “Having removed the attributes of the householder life” means having removed, thoroughly removed, laid down, and pacified the attributes of the householder life — that is 'having removed the attributes of the householder life'.

saṃhāyaṃ.meaning_2: companion who is wise; sagacious companion; intelligent friend
saṃhāyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is used as a gloss for nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ ('wise companion'), so it is treated here as an adjective. Could also be analysed as saha + aya, or as a commentarial variant of sahāya.
saṃhāyaṃ.example_1: Sace labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyanti sace nipakaṃ paṇḍitaṃ paññavantaṃ buddhimantaṃ ñāṇiṃ vibhāviṃ medhāviṃ sahāyaṃ labheyya paṭilabheyya adhigaccheyya vindeyyāti – sace labhetha nipakaṃ saṃhāyaṃ.
saṃhāyaṃ.translation_1: “If one should find a skillful companion” means if one should find, encounter, acquire, or experience a skillful, wise, intelligent, learned, knowledgeable, brilliant, and sagacious companion — that is 'if one should find a skillful companion'.

vīharaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads vīharaṃ, a variant of viharaṃ (present participle of viharati) with lengthened i; it agrees with the subject and means 'living, dwelling'. It is glossed alternatively as vihare, an optative.
vīharaṃ.translation_1: Lives in the wilderness as long as he wants, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

abhivajjetvā.meaning_2: having avoided; having shunned; having abandoned
abhivajjetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossing vivajjayitvā alongside parivajjetvā and abhinivajjetvā; absolutive in -tvā.
abhivajjetvā.example_1: nāgova yūthāni vivajjayitvāti yathā so hatthināgo yūthāni vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhinivajjetvā ekova araññavanamajjhogāhetvā carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpeti, paccekasambuddhopi gaṇaṃ vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhivajjetvā eko araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni.
abhivajjetvā.example_2: Nāgova yūthāni vivajjayitvāti yathā so hatthināgo yūthāni vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhinivajjetvā ekova araññavanamajjhogāhetvā [araññe vanamajjhassa ajjhogāhetvā (syā.)] carati viharati iriyati vatteti pāleti yapeti yāpeti, paccekasambuddhopi gaṇaṃ vivajjetvā parivajjetvā abhivajjetvā eko [eko care khaggavisāṇakappo (syā.)] araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni.
abhivajjetvā.translation_2: “Like an elephant, having abandoned the herds” — just as an elephant, having abandoned the herds, repeatedly avoiding, and constantly avoiding them, plunged into the forest, wanders, dwells, conducts itself, operates, keeps, lives, and survives, so too does a Solitary Awakened One, having abandoned the group, repeatedly avoiding, and constantly avoiding it, alone frequent the forest wildernesses, remote resting places, free from noise, free from sound, with their atmosphere devoid of people, appropriately secluded for resting undisturbed by human beings, and appropriate for seclusion.

āpātakajjhāyī.meaning_2: seeming to be absorbed in meditation; one who is like a meditator
āpātakajjhāyī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has āpāthakajjhāyī, but the variant reading āpātakajjhāyī (as given) is chosen. A compound describing someone who only appears to be meditating. The ending -ī is adjectival, referring to a person.
āpātakajjhāyī.example_1: Idhekacco pāpiccho icchāpakato sambhāvanādhippāyo ‘‘ evaṃ maṃ jano sambhāvessatī ’’ ti gamanaṃ saṇṭhapeti ṭhānaṃ saṇṭhapeti nisajjaṃ [nisajjanaṃ (ka.)] saṇṭhapeti sayanaṃ saṇṭhapeti, paṇidhāya gacchati paṇidhāya tiṭṭhati paṇidhāya nisīdati paṇidhāya seyyaṃ kappeti samāhito viya gacchati samāhito viya tiṭṭhati samāhito viya nisīdati samāhito viya seyyaṃ kappeti, āpāthakajjhāyīva [āpātakajjhāyī ca (ka.)] hoti.
āpātakajjhāyī.translation_1: Here, some person with evil desires, overwhelmed by greed, desiring to be admired, sets up his walking, sets up his standing, sets up his sitting, sets up his lying down; he walks having directed, stands having directed, sits having directed, lies down having directed, walks like someone composed, stands like someone composed, sits like someone composed, lies down like someone composed, and acts as one in meditative absorption.

saṃvantā.meaning_2: fully vomited; completely ejected; spewed out
saṃvantā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural masculine, qualifying makkho, kasāvo and moho: 'makkho ca ... moho ca ... vantā saṃvantā ...'. The PEU suggests saṃ + vamita, but the form is probably a prefix saṃ + vanta (pp of vamati), meaning 'fully vomited out'. The sandhi form saṃvantā is used.
saṃvantā.example_1: tassa paccekasambuddhassa makkho ca kasāvo ca moho ca vantā saṃvantā niddhantā pahīnā samucchinnā vūpasantā paṭippassaddhā abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāti.

tannino.meaning_2: inclined to that; disposed towards that; bent on that
tannino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the nominative singular form is tannino; the compound repeats the demonstrative taṃ of the preceding series (taccarito ... tadadhipateyyo), pointing back to kāme.
tannino.example_1: Pasutanti yopi kāme esati gavesati pariyesati taccarito tabbahulo taggaruko tannino tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyo, sopi kāmappasuto.
tannino.translation_1: ‘Engaged’ means: whoever searches for, seeks, and hunts for sensual pleasures, and is thus behaving, is thus habituated, is thus attentive, is thus inclined, is thus leaning, is thus leaning toward, is thus resolved, is thus subjected — he is engaged in sensuality.

saṃbhajeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular. In the text it glosses 'bhajeyya' as one of a series of near-synonyms (bhajeyya, seveyya, niseveyya, saṃseveyya, paṭiseveyya). Causative form, so the -e- before the optative ending.
saṃbhajeyya.example_1: Bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajethāti bahussutañca dhammadharañca mittaṃ bhajeyya saṃbhajeyya seveyya niseveyya saṃseveyya paṭiseveyyāti – bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ bhajetha.
saṃbhajeyya.translation_1: “You should follow a learned one, a holder of the Dhamma” means you should follow, associate with, serve, wait upon, keep company with, retreat with a friend who is both learned and a holder of the Dhamma — therefore one should follow a learned one, a holder of the Dhamma.

vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.meaning_2: place of adornment; occasion for decoration; cause of ornamentation
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular (or possibly a contraction of vibhūsanāya ṭhānā) in the verses; v.l. vibhūsaṭṭhānā, vibhūsanaṭṭhānā. Means grounds for adorning oneself, which one abstains from.
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.example_1: Vibhūsaṭṭhānā [vibhūsanaṭṭhānā (syā. ka.), vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā (sī. aṭṭha.)] virato saccavādī , eko care khaggavisāṇakappo .
vibhūsaṇaṭṭhānā.translation_1: Renounced from places of adornment, speaker of the truth, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

gaddhikatā.meaning_2: state of being greedy (for); craving; longing; attachment
gaddhikatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed in a pejorative series describing anāgārikavibhūsā (homeless vanity); variant reading gedhikatā. Nominative singular in the text.
gaddhikatā.example_1: cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ—
gaddhikatā.example_2: Cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā gaddhikatā gaddhikattaṃ [gedhikatā gedhikattaṃ (syā.) passa vibha.854] capalatā [capalanā (syā.)] cāpalyaṃ – ayaṃ anāgārikavibhūsā.
gaddhikatā.translation_2: Decoration of robes, decoration of the bowl, decoration of the lodging, decoration of this corpse-body or of external items, adornment, decoration, playing, playing in every way, yearning, bondage, frivolity, vanity — this is homeless adornment.

khetrajo.meaning_2: field-born son; son born from the field (i.e. of a wife of lower status); illegitimate son
khetrajo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative spelling (with r) of khettaja in the list of four kinds of sons; nominative singular in the text. The Thai edition reads khettajo.
khetrajo.example_1: Puttāti cattāro puttā – atrajo putto, khettajo [khetrajo (syā. ka.)] putto, dinnako putto, antevāsiko putto.
khetrajo.translation_1: “Sons” means there are four types of sons: the legitimate son, the field-born son, the adopted son, and the pupil son.

paṭippassambhitvāti.meaning_2: having calmed down; having become quiet; having subsided
paṭippassambhitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is followed by the enclitic -ti: paṭippassambhitvāti = paṭippassambhitvā + iti.
paṭippassambhitvāti.example_1: oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭippassambhitvāti sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ.
paṭippassambhitvāti.example_2: ohārayitvā gihibyañjanānīti gihibyañjanāni oropayitvā samoropayitvā nikkhipitvā paṭippassambhitvāti—

akuṭakaṃ.meaning_2: not bitter; free from bitterness; (what is) not acrid
akuṭakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative compound (na + kaṭuka, 'not bitter'); accusative singular neuter agreeing with the contrasted kaṭukaṃ. The na- prefix becomes a- before a consonant.
akuṭakaṃ.example_1: kaṭukaṃ labhitvā akuṭakaṃ pariyesanti, akuṭakaṃ labhitvā kaṭukaṃ pariyesanti;

udakummikajātaṃ.meaning_2: become like a water-wave; continuous like waves on water
udakummikajātaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant udakūmikajāta; explained in the gloss as poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ, i.e. continuous, wave upon wave. Nominative singular agreeing with dhammesu? no, with the practitioner; neuter/accusative usage uncertain, listed as adj.
udakummikajātaṃ.example_1: Dhammesu niccaṃ anudhammacārīti dhammesu niccakālaṃ dhuvakālaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ avokiṇṇaṃ poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ udakūmikajātaṃ [udakummijātaṃ (syā.), udakummikajātaṃ (ka.)]
udakummikajātaṃ.translation_1: “Constantly living in conformity with the Teaching” means, regarding those teachings, constantly, continuously, persistently, and without a break, one after another, like the waves on water,

paṭinisaṭṭhattā.meaning_2: state of having relinquished; state of having given up; detachment
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ā (paṭinisaṭṭhattā); abstract noun formed from the past participle paṭinisaṭṭha (relinquished, given up) + -tta, used here with diṭṭhilepa (taint of views).
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.example_1: taṇhālepassa pahīnattā diṭṭhilepassa paṭinisaṭṭhattā so paccekasambuddho rūpe na limpati sadde na limpati …pe…
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.example_2: Taṇhālepassa pahīnattā diṭṭhilepassa paṭinisaṭṭhattā so paccekasambuddho rūpe na limpati sadde na limpati … pe … diṭṭhasutamutaviññātabbesu dhammesu na limpati na palimpati na upalimpati, alitto apalitto anupalitto nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā viharatīti – padumaṃva toyena alimpamāno, eko care khaggavisāṇakappo.
paṭinisaṭṭhattā.translation_2: Because the taint of craving is abandoned and the taint of views is relinquished, that Solitary Awakened One does not taint forms, does not taint sounds… does not taint things seen, heard, sensed, and cognized, he does not taint, does not smear, does not adhere, untainted, undefiled, and untarnished; emerging, escaped, released, and detached, he dwells with a mind that has no limits—this is “like a lotus not soiled by water, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

nidveḷhakā.meaning_2: free from doubt; without hesitation; devoid of perplexity
nidveḷhakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it stands for nidveḷhakā, nominative plural, in the list of contrasts (sadveḷhakā → nidveḷhakā). The prefix ni- negates dveḷhaka (doubt, hesitation).
nidveḷhakā.example_1: kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti sakaṅkhā āgantvā nikkaṅkhā sampajjanti, sallekhā āgantvā nillekhā sampajjanti, sadveḷhakā āgantvā nidveḷhakā sampajjanti, savicikicchā āgantvā nibbicikicchā sampajjanti, sarāgā āgantvā vītarāgā sampajjanti, sadosā āgantvā vītadosā sampajjanti, samohā āgantvā vītamohā sampajjanti, sakilesā āgantvā nikkilesā sampajjantīti—
